topic.title: Model Armor
topic.docSection: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor & §5 Trigger #12
topic.summary: Floor settings, HIGH vs LOW_AND_ABOVE confidence, Inspect-only rollout, Basic vs Advanced SDP, 4 MB skip/no-bill limit, CSAM always-on, 40-URL limit, and OCR image screening.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor | Trigger #12 | M2S2 Slide 42
questions.q: A platform team wants every Model Armor template in the company to at least enable prompt-injection detection, while teams can still add stricter filters. What should they use?
options: Floor settings, which set minimum requirements at the org, folder, or project level that templates can't go below
One shared 'golden' template that every team must voluntarily reference
A confidence level of LOW_AND_ABOVE enforced via IAM Conditions
An IAM deny policy on the Model Armor API
questions.why: Floor settings define minimum enforcement requirements at the organization, folder, or project level. Teams can configure stricter filters on their templates, but cannot create a template less strict than the floor.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor | Trigger #12 | M2S2 Slide 44
questions.q: A customer complains that Model Armor blocks too many legitimate prompts. Which confidence level gives the FEWEST false positives?
options: HIGH (flags only high-likelihood violations, minimizing false positives)
LOW_AND_ABOVE (strictest setting, flags low, medium, and high)
MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE
Confidence level does not affect false-positive rates
questions.why: HIGH flags only high-confidence violations, resulting in the fewest false positives. LOW_AND_ABOVE is the strictest threshold and produces the most false positives.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor | Self-Test #5 & Trigger #12 | M2S2 Slide 49
questions.q: What is the recommended rollout sequence for a new Model Armor deployment?
options: Start in Inspect only, tune with test data, production monitoring, and user feedback, then switch to Inspect and block
Deploy straight to Inspect and block from day one, then relax filters if users complain
Keep Inspect only permanently, because blocking breaks LLM applications
Use Inspect and block for prompts and Inspect only for responses permanently
questions.why: Official best practice: start in Inspect only (logs findings without blocking), tune thresholds using test data, production telemetry, and feedback, and then switch to Inspect and block.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor | Trigger #12 (Swapped-Definition Trap) | M2S2 Slide 46
questions.q: A healthcare customer needs credit card numbers REDACTED or tokenized before prompts reach the model. What configuration do they need?
options: Advanced Sensitive Data Protection (SDP) configuration with an inspect template (required) and a de-identify template (optional)
Basic Sensitive Data Protection configuration (which automatically redacts US infoTypes)
The prompt-injection and jailbreak filter set to HIGH
A Responsible AI filter for 'dangerous content'
questions.why: Basic SDP uses a fixed set of predefined (mostly US) infoTypes and ONLY flags findings. Redaction or tokenization requires Advanced SDP with your own SDP inspect template (required) and de-identify template.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor | Self-Test #5 & Trigger #12 | M2S2 Slide 48
questions.q: A user uploads a 6 MB document for screening. What does Model Armor do?
options: Skips it (it isn't blocked), and the skipped data isn't billed
Blocks the file immediately because it exceeds the 4 MB limit
Compresses the file under 4 MB and then screens it
Splits the document into 4 MB chunks and screens each chunk
questions.why: Files and text over 4 MB are skipped (not blocked), and skipped data is not billed. Watch out for distractors claiming oversized files are blocked, compressed, or split.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor | Trigger #12 | M2S2 Slide 39
questions.q: A customer runs its LLM application on another cloud provider and on-premises. Can it use Model Armor?
options: Yes, Model Armor runs on any cloud or on-prem through its REST API
No, it only works with Vertex AI and Gemini on Google Cloud
Only if routed through GKE Enterprise on Google Cloud
Only for batch prediction workloads stored in BigQuery
questions.why: Model Armor is model- and cloud-agnostic: it can protect applications running on any cloud or on-premises via its REST API, as well as integrating natively with Apigee, Agent Gateway, Gemini Enterprise, and MCP servers.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor | Trigger #12 | M2S2 Slide 43
questions.q: Which Model Armor filter is ALWAYS applied by default and cannot be disabled?
options: CSAM (Child Sexual Abuse Material)
Hate speech
Prompt injection and jailbreak
Malicious URL detection
questions.why: CSAM detection is always on by default and cannot be turned off. The other four Responsible AI categories (hate speech, harassment, sexually explicit, dangerous content) have configurable thresholds.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor | M2S2 Slide 45
questions.q: A prompt contains 60 URLs. How many URLs does Model Armor's malicious URL detection scan?
options: The first 40 URLs
All 60 URLs
The first 10 URLs
None; URLs are only scanned in model responses
questions.why: Model Armor's malicious URL detection scans up to the first 40 URLs per input.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor | Trigger #12 | M2S2 Slides 49–50
questions.q: A CE is configuring Model Armor for a customer for the first time. Which starting configuration matches Google's recommended phased strategy?
options: Responsible AI filters at HIGH, prompt injection at MEDIUM (or HIGH for Gemini Enterprise), advanced SDP templates, in Inspect only mode
Responsible AI at LOW_AND_ABOVE, prompt injection at HIGH, basic SDP, in Inspect and block mode
All filters at LOW_AND_ABOVE with Inspect and block enabled on day one
Responsible AI disabled, CSAM disabled, and Inspect only mode
questions.why: Start in Inspect only with Responsible AI at HIGH (fewest false positives), prompt injection/jailbreak at MEDIUM (or HIGH for Gemini Enterprise), and advanced SDP templates before moving to Inspect and block.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor | M2S2 Slide 48
questions.q: Which statement about Model Armor IMAGE screening (Preview) is accurate?
options: Supports JPEG, PNG, and BMP only, up to 4 MB, one image per request, in US and EU multi-regions (using OCR)
Supports any image format up to 20 MB across all global regions
Scans up to 10 images per request for batch throughput
Only inspects EXIF image metadata, not visual text content
questions.why: Model Armor image screening supports JPEG, PNG, and BMP formats only, up to 4 MB, a single image per request, in US and EU multi-regions, extracting text via OCR.
